newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis, Palestinians clash over Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Israelis, Palestinians clash over Jerusalem.

text.p: Palestinians angered by Jewish settlement in Jerusalem threw petrol bombs and rocks at Israeli soldiers on Thursday in violence reminiscent of a six-year uprising ended by a peace deal now under fire.

Israeli troops responded with rubber bullets and teargas during clashes on the outskirts of Palestinian-ruled Bethlehem, southwest of Jerusalem. A hospital official said one protester was wounded and 14 were treated for teargas inhalation.

"What is taken by force, can only be taken back by force," said one protester. Palestinians also clashed with the Israeli army at the village of Bet Immar near Hebron. Soldiers fired teargas but no injuries were immediately reported.

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Dore Gold, an envoy from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, crossed paths in Cairo, the centre of Arab consultations on the crisis in Middle East peace talks.
Officials said Arafat would see Hosni Mubarak, while Gold would have talks with the Egyptian president's foreign policy adviser, Osama el-Baz.
"I'm here to convey a message from Israel to Egypt and we have a very new proposal about the peace process to discuss," Gold told reporters.
He was apparently referring to Netanyahu's offer to complete "final status" talks with the Palestinian Authority (PA) within six months, nearly two years earlier than planned.
The Palestinians have dismissed the plan as a trick. Netanyahu's communications director David Bar-Illan told Reuters Israel was hoping the PA would reexamine the proposal and change its stand.

But Palestinian negotiator Nabil Shaath said the Authority's priority was to stop Israel building settlements such as a project for 6,500 homes for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghenim, or Hor Homa, in East Jerusalem where ground was broken on Tuesday.

Israel occupied Arab East Jerusalem along with the rest of the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East War and considers all of the city its capital. The PA wants East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
In the Arab Silwan neighbourhood of East Jerusalem, five Jewish settler families moved into a sprawling house under the cover of darkness.

Since 1991 at least 18 settler families have moved into Silwan, home to 30,000 Palestinians. The area is just below the Old City walls where the biblical King David is said to have established the first capital of the Jewish people.
Netanyahu's office said a settler leader had informed him of the entry into Silwan but an official statement said the government did not initiate the action.
"Those people bought the houses with good money and they've just decided to move into them," Bar-Illan said.
Outside the tomb of the biblical Rachel north of Bethlehem, scores of Arab youths broke through Palestinian police lines to clash with Israeli soldiers guarding the shrine.
The violence lasted several hours before Palestinian police intervened and dispersed the demonstrators.

"This new intifada is because...Netanyahu is confiscating Palestinian land," said protester Samih Abu Ayyash, 28, referring to the uprising that erupted in the West Bank and Gaza in 1987 and ended with a 1993 Israel-PLO interim peace deal.

The militant Islamic group Hamas charged Arafat was blocking protesters from reaching Israeli-manned roadblocks to prevent the type of Jerusalem-related violence seen last September in which 61 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.
Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said army intelligence suggested the Palestinians would also initiate violence following weekly Moslem Friday prayers.

In Lebanon, Israeli jets hit Hizbollah guerrilla targets deep in northeast Lebanon near the Syrian border on Thursday, in apparent retaliation for the killing of an Israeli soldier by the guerrillas, security sources said.
